title: Ensure changes to system administration scope (sudoers) is collected
objective: Audit CIS checkpoint 6.3.3.1: Ensure changes to system administration scope (sudoers) is collected

playbook_input.description: Parameters the caller provides before execution

steps.name: Check if auditd is installed
steps.function: 1. Check if auditd is installed using command: `command -v auditctl`. Expected result: path to auditctl binary.

steps.name: Check on disk audit rules for /etc/sudoers and /etc/sudoers.d
steps.function: 2. Check on disk audit rules for /etc/sudoers and /etc/sudoers.d using command: `awk '/^ *-w/ &&/\/etc\/sudoers/ &&/ +-p *wa/ &&(/ key= *[!-~]* *$/||/ -k *[!-~]* *$/)' /etc/audit/rules.d/*.rules`. Expected result: `-w /etc/sudoers -p wa -k scope` and `-w /etc/sudoers.d -p wa -k scope`.

steps.name: Check loaded audit rules for /etc/sudoers and /etc/sudoers.d
steps.function: 3. Check loaded audit rules for /etc/sudoers and /etc/sudoers.d using command: `auditctl -l | awk '/^ *-w/ &&/\/etc\/sudoers/ &&/ +-p *wa/ &&(/ key= *[!-~]* *$/||/ -k *[!-~]* *$/)'`. Expected result: `-w /etc/sudoers -p wa -k scope` and `-w /etc/sudoers.d -p wa -k scope`.

steps.function: 4. Check overall compliance status: PASS if all previous checks pass, SKIP if auditd is not installed, FAIL if auditd is installed but rules are missing or incorrect.

compliance_constraints: Use failed_when: false on all audit tasks (except set_fact, debug) so all checks complete and report status
If the audit targets a specific software/service (e.g., GDM, GNOME, sshd, httpd), FIRST check if it is installed. If NOT installed, report SKIP for all checks.
This is an AUDIT playbook — it MUST NOT make any changes to the system. All tasks must be read-only (shell commands, stat, slurp, command with check-only flags, etc.).
reference_procedure:
On disk configuration
Run the following command to check the on disk rules:
# awk '/^ *-w/ \
&&/\/etc\/sudoers/ \
&&/ +-p *wa/ \
&&(/ key= *[!-~]* *$/||/ -k *[!-~]* *$/)' /etc/audit/rules.d/*.rules
Verify the output matches:
-w /etc/sudoers -p wa -k scope
-w /etc/sudoers.d -p wa -k scope
Running configuration
Run the following command to check loaded rules:
# auditctl -l | awk '/^ *-w/ \
&&/\/etc\/sudoers/ \
&&/ +-p *wa/ \
&&(/ key= *[!-~]* *$/||/ -k *[!-~]* *$/)'
Verify the output matches:
-w /etc/sudoers -p wa -k scope
-w /etc/sudoers.d -p wa -k scope
